code-architecture.entrypoints: The crate builds a `cargo-enforcer` binary (see Cargo.toml `[[bin]]`). `src/main.rs` is the thin CLI shell: it reads the subcommand argument (skipping the leading `enforcer` arg that cargo injects for `cargo enforcer <rule>`), parses it into a `Command`, and calls `command.run()`.
code-architecture.commands-dispatch: `src/t/command.rs` defines the `Command` enum. `Command::run` dispatches to each rule's module (e.g. `file_sizes::run()`). Adding a rule = new enum variant + new rule module.
code-architecture.shared-code: `src/s/` holds static data. `src/c/` is shared logic. `src/t/` is shared types.
code-architecture.rule-impls: Aside from the shared-code, each rule is implemented in its own folder under `src/rules` (Rules related to tree structure are grouped in `src/rules/tree_structure/`). In each folder, there is a description of the rule in desc.xml.
code-architecture.rule-anatomy: The conventional layout of a rule folder (see `mod_location`, `mod_over_file` for minimal examples): - `mod.rs` — declares the submodules and does `pub use main::run;`. - `main.rs` — `pub fn run() -> bool` is the entrypoint. It typically calls `scan::src_files(_check_file)` and hands the result to `report::print`. `run` returns `true` when the rule FAILED (any violations), matching `Command::run`. - `report.rs` — `print(passed, violations) -> bool`, wrapping `c::report::summary`. - Optional `t.rs` (or `t/`) for rule-local types; extra files/subfolders for bigger rules (e.g. `imports/verify/`, `calls/find/`). - Optional `fix/` (see `private_fn_naming`) — `pub fn fix()` applies the rule's automated fix in place. Wire it up by re-exporting it from the rule's `mod.rs` and adding an arm to `run::_fix`, which runs before the rule is checked when the user passes `--fix`. Wiring a new rule requires three edits beyond the folder: add `pub mod <name>;` to `src/rules/mod.rs`, a `Command` variant in `src/t/command.rs`, and a match arm in `src/run.rs`. Private fns are prefixed with `_` per the project convention.
code-architecture.rule-docs: Every rule folder carries: - `desc.xml` — the human spec of the rule. READ THIS FIRST when implementing or changing a rule — it is the source of truth for behavior.
code-architecture.shared-helpers: Reusable building blocks the rules lean on, so you rarely need bespoke fs/AST code: - `c::scan::src_files(rule)` — iterates every `.rs` under the existing src dirs (`s::EXISTING_SRC_DIRS`, i.e. `src` and `tests`), calling `rule(&Path) -> Outcome<V>` per file and tallying results into `(passed: usize, Vec<V>)`. - `t::Outcome<V>` — `Skipped | Passed | Failed(V)`; the return type of a per-file rule. `t::ItemsViolation { path: String, items: Vec<String> }` is the common violation payload (used by type/static/trait-location, etc.). - `c::files` — `rs(dir_name) -> Vec<PathBuf>` (glob), `parse(path) -> syn::File`. - `c::path` — `rel(path)` (root-relative display string), `under_dir(path, name)` (any path component equals `name`), `common_file_kind(path)` (`Some("c"|"cnst"|"s"|"t" |"ext_traits")` when the file stem is a common name), `parent_name`, `is_mod_or_lib`. Common dirs/files are the five names `c, cnst, s, t, ext_traits`. - `c::ast` — `is_public(vis)`, plus `use`-tree helpers (`glob_module`, `exposed_names`). AST work uses the `syn` crate (`syn::Item::*`, etc.). - `c::report::summary(name, passed, success_msg, violations, on_fail)` — prints the cyan header, the green success line or the pass/fail counts, and invokes `on_fail` to render details. Use `colored::Colorize` for coloring (`.bold()`, `.red()`…).
code-architecture.enforcer.toml: `src/s/file_config.rs` exposes the `FILE_CONFIG` static: a `LazyLock` that reads `enforcer.toml` from the project root (`ROOT`), allows users to configure the rules. The top-level `debug` flag (default false) controls output verbosity: see std-out.
code-architecture.std-out:
With `debug = true` in enforcer.toml, every rule prints a full report: nice color schemes following the pattern already laid out, a message of the "all passed" sort if all pass, and if failures the details, so the user knows where the failures happened and can click links, if possible, to go fix. The number of passes and failures is printed in all cases, like it is for the existing rules.
With debug off (the default), passing rules print nothing at all: only failing rules print their report, and if every rule passes a single `[Success] All rules passed` line is printed by `run::rules`.
